nonLabourLines.description: CI/staging environment and cloud infra costs
Contingency for third-party services (email, search, tracing tools)

assumptions: The provided rate card (75 USD/hour, 1 FTE, generic 'Team member') is a placeholder — no real team members, roles, or negotiated rates exist yet. All costs here are indicative only and MUST be re-estimated once actual staff are assigned roles (e.g. backend, frontend, QA, DevOps) and their real hourly rates are known.

No historical actuals (real spend/velocity data) exist for this project or team, so effort has been estimated purely from story points using an assumed points-to-hours conversion (1 point ≈ 6 hours of blended effort, informed by task descriptions and typical complexity), not from empirical throughput.

Only one role ('Team member') is available on the rate card at 1 FTE (i.e. one person, ~40 hrs/week, ~2080 hrs/year). The backlog totals ~2413 hours of estimated effort, which exceeds a single FTE's annual capacity (roughly 1.16 work-years) — this role is staffed far too thinly for the full backlog and either headcount must increase, timeline must extend (~14+ months sequentially), or scope must shrink.

Story points were converted to hours as: 5 pts ≈ 30 hrs, 8 pts ≈ 48 hrs, 13 pts ≈ 78 hrs, 21 pts ≈ 126 hrs, reflecting typical relative sizing, then summed across all 24 backlog items and lightly adjusted upward (~10%) for integration/testing overhead not captured in individual task points.

Non-labour costs (CI/cloud infra, Stripe/PCI setup, Oracle migration tooling, misc third-party service contingency) are rough placeholders since no vendor quotes were supplied; actuals will vary once vendors/tools are selected.

Scenario spread (Optimistic/Most Likely/Pessimistic) reflects estimation uncertainty typical of early-stage backlogs with no actuals: -12% for best case (fewer unknowns in migration/integration) and +21% for worst case (legacy migration, multi-currency, and Stripe reconciliation are historically prone to overruns).
Priority breakdown costs are apportioned pro-rata from each task's estimated hours multiplied by the single blended rate, since no per-role cost differentiation exists yet.
input.reasoning: Effort was sized per backlog item from story points using an approximate 1 point = 6 hours blended-effort heuristic (adjusted for described complexity, e.g. legacy migration and payment integration carry extra risk buffer), then summed to ~2413 hours across all 24 items. Since the only available rate card entry is a single placeholder 'Team member' role at $75/hr with 1 FTE, all labour was costed against that one line, explicitly flagging that 1 FTE cannot realistically absorb ~2413 hours of work within a normal timeframe (it implies over a year of continuous solo effort), so either more headcount/roles need to be added to the rate card or the timeline/scope must adapt. Non-labour costs were added for infrastructure, third-party integration (Stripe/PCI), legacy migration tooling, and general service contingency, based on typical costs for comparable engagements since no vendor quotes were given. Three scenarios (P10/P50/P90) were produced to reflect the wide uncertainty inherent in a backlog with no historical actuals and significant unknowns (large-scale legacy data migration, multi-currency settlement, payment reconciliation). A priority-based cost breakdown was derived by allocating each task's cost by its assigned priority label. Cost-reduction options focus on descoping/deferring low-priority backlog items and trimming buffer/contingency, since headcount and rate are fixed by the placeholder card.

reductions.description: Defer low-priority items PW-12 (Support ticket submission), PW-18 (Admin back-office), PW-19 (Usage analytics), PW-23 (Contract tests), and PW-24 (Decommission legacy portal) to a later phase — none block the core customer-facing launch.
reductions.effect: Removes ~39 points (~316 hours) of low-priority backlog from this phase; portal can launch without them and they can be scheduled post-launch.

reductions.description: Descope multi-currency support (PW-14) to USD-only at launch, adding EUR/PLN later once volume justifies it.
reductions.effect: Removes 13 points (~78 hours) of complex FX/settlement work from the initial release.

reductions.description: Reduce non-labour contingency line for third-party services from $2,500 to $1,000 by confirming actual vendor pricing (email/search/tracing tools) before committing budget.
reductions.effect: Tighter non-labour estimate once real vendor quotes replace the placeholder contingency; risk shifts to a change request if quotes come in higher.

reductions.description: Phase the legacy data migration (PW-8) into a smaller pilot migration (e.g. 10% of records) for initial launch, with full migration following in a second pass once validated.
reductions.effect: Cuts an estimated 21 points (~126 hours) down to a lighter pilot-scope migration (~50 hours), deferring the remaining ~76 hours; reduces risk of a costly one-shot migration failure.
